&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 210 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The stretch of dry and quiet weather will persist across 
the region as high pressure continues to build into the region, with 
the center of the high overhead tomorrow into Sunday before 
gradually shifting eastward. Ideal radiational cooling conditions 
will allow for some cold overnight lows tonight, with temperatures 
dropping into the teens and 20s, likely a few degrees cooler than 
the last few nights. Temperatures will gradually moderate throughout 
the weekend, with high temperatures warming into the lower 60s for 
Sunday and Monday. Dewpoints will be fairly low, dropping into the 
20s or so, but no fire weather concerns are anticipated given the 
lack of winds across the region with the high pressure overhead. A 
weak cold front looks to move through the region on Monday, but with 
such dry air ahead of the feature and lack of moisture, no 
precipitation is expected just a slight increase in cloud cover.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Our prolonged period of dry weather will continue 
through at least the middle part of next week as sprawling high 
pressure returns on Tuesday. Longer range models continue to show 
another cold frontal passage late week, accompanied by light QPF. 
Given the lack of a deep plume of moisture ahead of this front, 
wouldn't be surprised if we get nothing but a period of increased 
cloud cover, much like our frontal passage yesterday. Still, it's a 
week out, so have stayed with the NBM/WPC forecast for now, which 
gives low chances of showers late next week. Temperatures will 
remain seasonable, coolest on Tuesday but warming as the week 
progresses.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 18Z Saturday...VFR conditions will prevail through the entire
TAF period as high pressure settles overhead. Skies to remain SKC-
FEW250 for the next 24 hours. N/NW (except NE at MSS) winds 5-10 kt
this afternoon becoming light and variable after 22z this evening,
remaining so through Saturday morning.
